Hours & Location

Contact lenses have come a long way — and so have the people who wear them. With modern advances in lens design and materials, it’s easier than ever to find contacts that match your vision, your comfort level, and your day-to-day lifestyle. The key is knowing your options — and getting professionally fitted.

Whether you're active, on screens all day, or just ready to ditch your glasses, there's a contact lens out there that can work for you. And at Briargrove Eye Center, we're here to help you find it.

The Main Types of Contact Lenses Explained

Not sure where to start? Here’s a breakdown of the most common types of contact lenses — each designed for a different need:

  • Daily contacts: Worn once and thrown away — a fresh lens every day means ultimate hygiene and minimal maintenance. Great for allergy sufferers or anyone with a busy schedule.
  • Monthly lenses: Designed for reuse over 30 days with proper care. They’re cost-effective and a favorite for those who prefer routine.
  • Toric lenses: Specifically made to correct astigmatism. These lenses have unique shapes that help align your vision correctly throughout the day.
  • Multifocal contact lenses: For patients who need help seeing both near and far — often used for age-related vision changes (presbyopia).
  • Specialty lenses: Custom options for dry eyes, keratoconus, or other irregularities in the shape of the cornea.

How to Choose the Right Contact Lenses

Picking the right contacts isn’t just about vision correction — it’s about fit, comfort, and function.

That’s why we start every contact lens fitting at Briargrove Eye Center with a full evaluation of:

  • Your eye health
  • Corneal shape and tear quality
  • Your day-to-day lifestyle (screen time, outdoor activity, sports, allergies)

Maybe you work long hours in front of a screen or need lenses that can keep up with gym time and weekend travel. Maybe your current lenses dry out by lunch. Whatever your routine, we’ll help you find a lens that actually fits your life.

Why Proper Fitting Matters

A good contact lens fit isn’t just about comfort — it’s essential for eye health. Poorly fitted lenses can cause irritation, dryness, or even damage to the surface of your eye. That’s why our contact lens fitting process is so thorough.

We’ll match you with the best lens based on:

  • Your lifestyle and vision goals
  • The shape and condition of your corneas
  • How your eyes respond to lens materials

Most patients can try on lenses during the same visit as their eye exam — and you may even go home with a few daily contacts or monthly options to test before making a final decision.

Follow-up fittings matter too. Our eye care team checks in after your trial to see how things are going, adjust the lens if needed, and make sure you’re confident in care and hygiene. We’ll teach you proper handling and explain what to watch out for — so you can wear your contacts safely and comfortably long term.

Tips for First-Time Contact Lens Wearers

New to contacts? No sweat. Here’s what to know as you get started:

  • Always wash your hands before inserting or removing lenses
  • Start with shorter wear times and increase gradually
  • Avoid sleeping in lenses unless approved by your optometrist
  • Stick to the cleaning routine recommended for your lens type
  • Use fresh solution daily — never top off old liquid
  • Stay consistent with replacement schedules (especially for daily contacts and monthlies)

When to Replace or Reassess Your Lenses

It might be time to change your contacts if:

  • You’re experiencing more dryness or discomfort
  • Your vision isn’t as clear as it used to be
  • Your lifestyle has changed (e.g., more travel, screen time, or sports)
  • You’ve had changes in your prescription
  • You’re just not loving how your lenses feel anymore

Schedule Your Contact Lens Fitting in Houston

Whether you're new to lenses or looking for something better than your current brand, Briargrove Eye Center makes the process easy.

We offer:

  • Personalized fittings with experienced optometrists
  • A full range of brands and materials — including toric lenses and multifocal contact lenses
  • Convenient follow-ups to make sure your contacts are working for you
